subject: [Bugfix][ROCm] Change AttentionCGSuppoort in TritonMLA to UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE (#47144)
pr_body:
## Purpose
TritonMLAMetadataBuilder advertised _cudagraph_support = AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH (added in #42885) while keeping the inherited query_len_support = SINGLE_ONLY (so reorder_batch_threshold = 1).

With speculative decoding enabled, the UNIFORM_BATCH claim bypasses a downgrade in resolve_cudagraph_mode_and_sizes (which only triggers when min_cg_support < UNIFORM_BATCH). 
Full decode cudagraph capture then proceeds with max_query_len = 2 and trips the decode-only assertion in `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.build_for_cudagraph_capture`:
```
assert m.max_query_len <= self.reorder_batch_threshold  # decode only
```
This surfaced in ROCm CI because without the AITER MLA kernel, TritonMLA is the only one available in the case of the failing model. For Nvidia, the TritonMLA doesn't get selected so the issue didn't present itself.
## Test Plan
pytest "tests/models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[EagleDeepSeekMTPModel]"

## Test Result
Previously the test failed by tripping the aforementioned assert, now it passes.

---

subject: Fix NaN in triton EAGLE spec-v2 draft-extend CUDA graph at topk>1 (wrong qo_indptr stride) (#27545)
pr_body:
The draft-extend CUDA-graph metadata built `qo_indptr` with a per-req stride of `num_steps+1`, but the runner lays out `num_draft_tokens` tokens/req. For topk>1 these differ, so at bs>1 each req's queries read from the wrong offset -> NaN (bs==1 and eager are unaffected). Use `num_draft_tokens` for the v2 draft-extend path.

subject: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Register the offload region in chunks (#51081)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51080.

`pin_mmap_region` registered the whole offload region with one `cudaHostRegister` call. A single registration of 512 GiB or more fails with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` no matter how much host memory is free, so `cpu_bytes_to_use` at or above ~550e9 is never pinned. Measured on 4×H200 NVL with 1.3 TB free, one process, no model loaded:

| region size | result |
|---|---|
| 20 / 300 / 400 / 500 GB | success, ~0.1 s per GB |
| 549.7e9 (511.96 GiB) | success, 55.4 s |
| 549.9e9 (512.15 GiB) | **fails, code=2** |
| 600e9 | fails, code=2 |

This became reachable with #50094: before it each rank pinned its own `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size` buffer, all far below the ceiling; after it one shared region is registered in full by every rank.

A failed registration also leaves its error pending on the thread, and the next error check in torch reports it against an unrelated call. That is how this surfaced for us: a bogus `AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory` in `warm_v1_block_table_kernels`, and a worker that did not start.

## Changes

- Register the region in chunks of at most 64 GiB that end on block-row boundaries. Rows are page aligned, so the driver's page rounding never makes two registrations overlap and no block transfer spans a boundary. A single row larger than the cap is registered whole.
- Registration is all or nothing. On a failed chunk, drain the pending error and unregister the chunks registered before it, so `region.is_pinned` means the whole region is pinned. The cost is that a failure on the last chunk leaves the whole region on the pageable path; in exchange nothing downstream has to track a partly pinned region.
- Register, drain and roll back through one `CudaRTLibrary` instance. `torch.cuda.cudart()` has no `cudaGetLastError` binding, so the drain cannot go through torch. `CudaRTLibrary` gains `cudaHostRegister`, `cudaHostUnregister` and `cudaGetLastError` with their HIP names; this part comes from #50070 and its author is credited as co-author. If the runtime library cannot be loaded, the region stays pageable instead of failing worker startup.
- Cleanup of a fully registered region is unchanged: it releases `pinn …[truncated]

subject: [Bugfix] Mamba2 SSD varlen bug fix initstates decay, improve test, assert chunk pwr 2 (#21783)
pr_body:
## Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist

## Purpose
This PR fixes a correctness bug for varlen Mamba2 SSD (prefill). 

Some of the existing tests required a high tolerance such as 50% rtol (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/21379), and a larger test of 768 tokens and 128 chunk_size failed (other tests seem to be only 64 tokens). These issues are fixed in this PR.

Here is an instinctive explanation of the bug:
1. There was an unnecessary offset in reading `dA_cs_m_boundary`, causing a "later" (more decay) value to be read if `BLOCK_SIZE_M` < `chunk_size`
2. The effective `dA` which was offset (subtract) by `dA_cs_m_boundary` and was therefore "earlier" (less decay)
3. The `scale_m` was therefore off, representing less decay
4. The `prev_states` or `initstates` would have too much influence on the current token due to `scale_m`

Note: we require that chunk_size is a power of 2. The chunk_size does not affect correctness and can be tuned for performance, so it's not useful to have a non-power-of-2 chunk_size since Triton tensors would anyway need to be padded to powers of 2. One of the test cases was removed, and one was adjusted to use chunk_size=16 instead of 17.

After these changes, all tests pass. The `test_mamba_chunk_scan_cont_batch` tests that used to have 50% rtol in some cases now all use `atol, rtol = 5e-3, 5e-3` and the corresponding `if` and `TODO` were removed.

## Test Plan
Add new larger test size, remove a bad test, adjust a bad test, fix tolerances, and run:
` pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py `
## Test Result
All tests pass
`342 passed in 933.16s (0:15:33)`
## (Optional) Documentation Update
None, but an assert will trigger if chunk_size is not a power of 2. This probably does not need to be documented, especially given the assertion message `chunk_size must be integer power of 2`.

subject: [ROCm][Bugfix] Use token-level KV indices in the aiter ASM context-prefill gather (#36852)
pr_body:
## Motivation

#36758 added an ASM fp8 varlen path for context-chunk prefill on gfx950, and at
the default `--page-size 1` it is a solid win: measured +4-10% end-to-end
throughput and a 5-9% TTFT reduction at 60k input on Qwen3.8-2.4T with TP8. This PR
extends it to `page_size > 1`, where we ran into accuracy issues due to an indexing mismatch.

The gather derives its pool slots like this:
`aiter_backend.py`:
```python
page_slot = kv_indptr[seq_ids].to(torch.long) + pos_in_seq // page
tok_idx = kv_pages[page_slot].to(torch.long) * page + pos_in_seq % page
```

That treats `kv_indptr` / `kv_indices` as page-granular. As far as I can tell they
are actually token-level at every page size, even when the allocator is
page-based: `AiterIndicesUpdaterPrefill` builds `kv_indptr = cumsum(seq_lens)` and
`create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` writes one `kv_indices` entry per token. So
token `t` of sequence `i` is already at pool slot `kv_indices[kv_indptr[i] + t]`,
with no page indirection to undo. There is a comment a few hundred lines up in the
same file that says:

```python
# Non-unified AITER CUDA graph paths fill this buffer with flat
# token-level kv_indices via create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton
# (kv_indptr = cumsum(seq_lens)).  Even when the allocator is
# page-based, these writes are per-token, [...]
# TODO(aiter, page_size>1): root fix is to make page_size>1
# actually engage the attention kernel [...]
```

At `page_size=1` the two readings are the same expression (`t // 1 == t`,
`t % 1 == 0`, `slot * 1 == slot`), so the default path is exactly right and
nothing about the configuration #36758 benchmarked changes. Above 1 it goes one
of two ways depending on how full the KV pool is:

- the computed `tok_idx` leaves the pool, the second bounds check catches it, and
  we fall back to `ck_tile` - correct results, but the ASM path never engages;
- the computed `tok_idx` happens to stay inside the pool, both checks pass, and
  attention reads from the wrong slots.

## Modifications

Index the token table directly:
```python
kv_slot = kv_indptr[seq_ids] + pos_in_seq
tok_idx = kv_indices[kv_slot].to(torch.long)
```

subject: elastic_ep: Fix issues with repeated scale up/down cycles (#37131)
pr_body:
This PR fixes two issues found when testing repeated scale up/down cycles:

1. PyNCCL communicators were never explicitly destroyed during
elastic EP reconfigurations. Over repeated scale up/down cycles,
this causes CUDA OOM crashes. Fixed by cleaning up PyNCCL correctly.

2. Elastic EP EPLB suppression was scattered across executor, worker, and
state-machine code, which made its lifecycle hard to follow and caused
bugs such as EPLB staying suppressed after scale down. Fixed by making
elastic_execute the sole owner of EPLB suppression.

While removing EPLB suppression from load_model, also clean up the
entire Elastic EP new-worker load path which was extremely messy:
Move EEP-specific logic from GPUWorker.load_model() into
elastic_execute, go through the same executor load path for both
regular and EEP new workers, and move the remaining scale-up logic,
such as receive_weights, into the elastic state machine where it belongs
(symmetric to existing-worker send_weights)

subject: [Bugfix] DeepEP-V2: expert_tokens_meta must be None on the decode/cudagraph path (empty recv_expert_num_tokens) (#52632)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a deterministic startup crash in graph-enabled (default-compilation) serving with `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`.

In `DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize._receiver`, `expert_tokens_meta` was built unconditionally via `mk.ExpertTokensMetadata.make_from_list(recv_expert_num_tokens, ...)`. On the decode/cudagraph path, `do_cpu_sync = not self.use_cudagraph` (this file) intentionally skips the CPU sync, leaving `recv_expert_num_tokens` **empty** — so the call builds a **present-but-empty** `ExpertTokensMetadata`. That violates the decode-mode contract documented at the top of this file (`expert_tokens_meta` must be `None` when counts are absent), and downstream it crashes DeepEP's `combine` during startup `profile_run`.

Measured, two independent reproductions of the same call path (`profile_run → finalize_async → DeepEP elastic.py combine`):
- H200/B200, EP16 (DP16, 2 nodes over EFA, NCCL-GIN CPU proxy): Triton illegal-memory-access at `deepep_v2.py` combine, 12+/16 ranks, deterministic ~48 s into startup, 2/2 repro (Xid 43, ECC clean).
- Independently reproduced by AWS on B300, EP16, DeepSeek-V2-Lite BF16: `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED (719)` raised from DeepEP's JIT handle at the same phase — one root cause surfacing at different synchronization points.

`--enforce-eager` avoids the crash (the sync happens); this guard makes default compilation safe.

## Changes

One guard: return `expert_tokens_meta = None` when `recv_expert_num_tokens` is empty (the decode/cudagraph path), matching the documented contract; the prefill path (`do_cpu_sync=True`) is unchanged.

## Test Plan / Validation

- With the guard applied at `e2f993dc4`-era pins: graph-enabled `vllm serve` (no `--enforce-eager`) on EP16/DP16 across 2 nodes over EFA completes CUDA-graph capture, reaches `Application startup complete`, and serves: 153/153 HTTP 200 across a 1/8/16/32/64 concurrency sweep (previously: deterministic crash in `profile_run` before startup completed).
- Eager path unaffected (guard only changes the empty-list case).

subject: [fix] Skip routed expert capture for draft model under spec v2 (#26980)
pr_body:
## Summary
Stop a speculative draft from polluting the target's routed-experts capture.

## Symptom & Reproduction
- **Symptom:** With `--enable-return-routed-experts` plus a MoE draft (NextN / MTP / EAGLE-MoE), returned `routed_experts` diverge from the target-only baseline.
- **Reproduction:** `python -m pytest test/registered/rl/test_return_routed_experts_mtp.py` (Qwen3-30B-A3B target + Qwen3-MoE EAGLE3 draft vs target-only baseline).

## Root Cause
1. `RoutedExpertsCapturer` is a process-global singleton: one target-sized buffer keyed by `layer_id`.
2. A speculative draft `ModelRunner` runs in the same process as its target.
3. Draft MoE `TopK`, `init_routed_experts_capturer`, `forward`'s `on_forward_end` all reach that one capturer with no draft/target distinction.
4. Draft writes land in the target's buffer, so returned `routed_experts` carry draft ids over the target-only result.

## Fix
- `TopKConfig.allow_routed_experts_capture` (default `True`) gates the single capture site `capture_routed_experts_if_allowed`, called by both the CUDA `_post_process_topk_ids` / NPU `fused_topk_npu` paths.
- `ModelRunner.initialize` calls `disable_routed_experts_capture_for_draft(self.model)` on every draft worker, flipping that flag `False` on each draft `TopK` before any backend/graph init.
- The BYPASS piecewise-cuda-graph path threads the flag through its custom-op signature, then its rebuilt `TopKConfig`.
- `init_routed_experts_capturer` early-returns for a draft worker, so it never reinstalls the global capturer.
- `forward` gates `on_forward_end` on `not self.is_draft_worker`.

## Review Focus
- Scrutinize that `capture_routed_experts_if_allowed` is the only capture site; a direct capturer write bypasses the flag.
- Scrutinize the BYPASS path, where the flag is rebuilt from scalar args rather than carried on the module.
- Scrutinize that `disable_routed_experts_capture_for_draft` runs before any graph/backend init in `initialize`.
